arxiv-2111-05762.title: Non-dimensional Newton-Puiseux Expansions
arxiv-2111-05762.creator: C. J. Chapman
arxiv-2111-05762.description: Abstract Recent results in the theory and application of Newton-Puiseux expansions, i.e. fractional power series solutions of equations, suggest further developments within a more abstract algebraic-geometric framework, involving in particular the theory of toric varieties and ideals. Here, we present a number of such developments, especially in relation to the equations of van der Pol, Riccati, and Schrödinger.

arxiv-2205-10067.title: Island and lake size distributions in Gradient Percolation
arxiv-2205-10067.creator: S. S. Manna
arxiv-2205-10067.description: Abstract The well known problem of gradient percolation has been revisited to study the probability distribution of island sizes. It is observed that like the ordinary percolation, this distribution is also described by a power law decaying function but the associated critical exponents are found to be different.

arxiv-2302-02776.title: Calculation of true coincidence summing correction factor for a Broad Energy Germanium (BEGe) detector using standard and fabricated sources
arxiv-2302-02776.creator: Ashish Gupta, M. Shareef, Munmun Twisha, Saikat Bhattacharjee, Gopal Mukherjee, Satya Samiran Nayak, Sansaptak Basu, S. Dasgupta, J. Datta, S. Bhattacharyya, A. Mukherjee
arxiv-2302-02776.description: Abstract The true coincidence summing (TCS) correction factor for a Broad Energy Germanium (BEGe) detector has been calculated at far and close geometry measurement using multi-energetic radioactive γ \gamma -ray sources 60 Co, 133 Ba and 152 Eu. The correction factors were calculated using experimental method and analytical method.

arxiv-2306-11989.title: Superheavy Elements and Ultradense Matter
arxiv-2306-11989.creator: Evan LaForge, Will Price, Johann Rafelski
arxiv-2306-11989.description: Abstract In order to characterize the mass density of superheavy elements, we solve numerically the relativistic Thomas-Fermi model of an atom. To obtain a range of mass densities for superheavy matter, this model is supplemented with an estimation of the number of electrons shared between individual atoms.

arxiv-2412-13833.title: Multiple reflections on Huygens’ principle
arxiv-2412-13833.creator: Kees Wapenaar Department of Geoscience and Engineering, Delft University of Technology, The Netherlands
arxiv-2412-13833.description: Abstract According to Huygens’ principle, all points on a wave front act as secondary sources emitting spherical waves, and the envelope of these spherical waves forms a new wave front. In the mathematical formulation of Huygens’ principle, the waves emitted by the secondary sources are represented by Green’s functions.

pmc-11461069.title: Long-term anti-predator learning and memory differ across populations and sexes in an intertidal snail
pmc-11461069.creator: Isabelle P. Neylan, Emily K. Longman, Eric Sanford, John J. Stachowicz, Andrew Sih
pmc-11461069.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Anti-predator behaviours in response to predator cues can be innate, or they can be learned through prior experience and remembered over time. The duration and strength of continued anti-predator behaviour after predator cues are no longer present, and the potential for an enhanced response when re-exposed to predator cues later is less known but could account for the observed variation in anti-predator responses.

pmc-11547992.title: Tracking Long-Lived Free Radicals in Dandelion Caused by Air Pollution Using Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
pmc-11547992.creator: Ireneusz Stefaniuk, Bogumił Cieniek, Agata Ćwik, Katarzyna Kluska, Idalia Kasprzyk
pmc-11547992.description: Studies on particulate air pollution indicate that a new type of pollutant should be considered from mainly fossil fuel combustion and automobile exhaust emissions, i.e., environmentally persistent free radicals. These radicals, ubiquitous in the environment, have a long life span and are capable of producing harmful reactive oxygen species.

pmc-12361438.description: Vertebrate inner ear mechanosensory hair cells detect sound and gravitational forces. Additionally, fishes have homologous lateral line hair cells in the skin that detect water vibrations for orientation and predator avoidance. Hair cells in the lateral line and ear of fishes and other non-mammalian vertebrates regenerate readily after damage, but mammalians lack this ability, causing deafness and vestibular defects.

pmc-12532928.title: The impact of Pecha Kucha on enhancing basic life support training: randomized controlled trial
pmc-12532928.creator: Maide Yeşilyurt
pmc-12532928.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundBasic Life Support (BLS) is essential for saving lives, yet traditional teaching methods may not ensure lasting learning. Pecha Kucha, a dynamic and visual presentation style, has been suggested to boost engagement and retention. This study aimed to determine the effect of Basic Life Support (BLS) training given with the Pecha Kucha (PK) method on the level of learning and practicing Basic Life Support among students studying health services.MethodsA randomized controlled study was conducted according to the CONSORT guideline.

pmc-12557987.title: Effect of perioperative intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium in elderly hip fracture patients undergoing general anesthesia: a randomized controlled study

pmc-12557987.description: ObjectivePostoperative delirium (POD) frequently occurs among elderly patients following surgery, yet effective preventive measures remain insufficiently established. pmc-13572208.title: Robotic Distal Gastrectomy with D2 Lymphadenectomy for Gastric Cancer in a Patient with an Unclassifiable Celiac Arterial Anomaly: A Case Report
pmc-13572208.creator: Kohei Fujita, Hiroyuki Sagawa, Shigeyuki Kosaka, Shohei Hayashi, Eri Tsuji, Shunsuke Hayakawa, Sunao Ito, Reo Sato, Ryo Ogawa, Shuji Takiguchi
pmc-13572208.description: INTRODUCTIONSuprapancreatic lymph node dissection during gastric cancer surgery is technically challenging, particularly in the presence of celiac arterial system–related vascular anomalies. However, some rare arterial configurations do not clearly fit within existing classification systems, making surgical planning difficult. Herein, we report a case of gastric cancer with an unclassifiable celiac arterial anomaly that was managed using a robotic approach.

uslaw-usc-t15-s1681f.title: 15 U.S.C. § 1681f — Disclosures to governmental agencies
uslaw-usc-t15-s1681f.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s1681f.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 41 (Consumer Credit Protection); Subchapter III (Credit Reporting Agencies). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding the provisions of section 1681b of this title, a consumer reporting agency may furnish identifying information respecting any consumer, limited to his name, address, former addresses, places of employment, or former places of employment, to a governmental agency.
